cli.cmd.local: Review the current branch against its base on this machine. Nothing is posted.
cli.cmd.doctor: Check git and the harnesses you have, and what each one can do.
cli.opt.base: Base ref to compare with (default: detected from origin).
cli.opt.uncommitted: Also review uncommitted changes to tracked files.
cli.opt.harness: Harness: auto, claude, codex, kiro, or one from your config.
cli.opt.verifierHarness: Harness for the verifier (default: the same as --harness).
cli.opt.lens: Run only these lenses, comma-separated. The verdict is then partial.
cli.opt.noVerify: Skip the verifier: faster, more false alarms.
cli.opt.lang: Language of the findings (default: your config, then your system language).
cli.opt.conformance: With doctor: run a real two-prompt test on each harness (uses a little quota).
error.noBase: Couldn't find a base branch. Pass one with --base.
error.diffTooLarge: The change has {lines} changed lines, over the limit of {limit} (limits.maxDiffLines).
error.noHarness: No harness installed. Install Claude Code, Codex or Kiro, or add one to your config, then run crewreview doctor.
error.harnessNotReadOnly: {name} can't be locked to read-only, so it can't review. Pick another harness.
error.needsConformance: {name} hasn't passed the read-only test yet. Run crewreview doctor --conformance first.
error.allLensesFailed: Every lens failed. See the errors above.
doctor.title: Crewreview doctor
doctor.seatMissing: Seat {seat} uses {harness}, which isn't installed here: its jobs go to the next seat.
doctor.conformanceHint: Run crewreview doctor --conformance to prove the read-only lock with a real run.
doctor.notReady: Not ready: no installed harness can review.
local.title: Crewreview · local review
local.droppedEvidence.one: {count} finding dropped for citing a file or line that doesn't exist.
local.droppedEvidence.other: {count} findings dropped for citing a file or line that doesn't exist.
local.leftOut: Left out (minified, generated or too large to read): {files}
local.guidelinesCut: Project rules read only in part (too long): {files}
local.reviewGuide: Followed the team's review guidance in {file}
reason.blocking-findings: a verified finding blocks the merge
reason.unverified-blockers: a blocker was found but not verified
reason.findings-block-approval: some findings are too serious to approve
reason.lens-failed: a lens failed or didn't cover everything
reason.diff-too-large: the change is too large to approve automatically
status.hallucinated: discarded: cited files that don't exist
cli.cmd.repo: Link, list, change or remove the repositories, or whole organizations, the crew watches.
cli.cmd.task: Give the crew a task: it plans, you approve, it builds step by step, reviews itself and opens a pull request.
cli.cmd.once: Check every linked repository once and review what's due.
cli.cmd.run: Keep checking linked repositories until you stop it (Ctrl+C).
cli.opt.mode: off, inbox (waits for your approval) or auto (posts right away). Default: inbox.
cli.opt.authors: Whose pull requests to review: others, all or mine. Default: others.
cli.opt.kind: For self-hosted instances whose address doesn't say github or gitlab.
cli.opt.clone: A clone on this machine to borrow objects from on the first fetch.
cli.opt.id: A short name for the repository (default: from its path).
cli.opt.post: Post right away instead of sending the review to the inbox.
cli.opt.dryRun: Only print the review. Nothing is saved or posted.
cli.opt.force: Review even if this commit was already reviewed.
error.noToken: No token for {host}. Sign in with {cli} auth login, or set {env}.
error.unknownRepo: No linked repository called {id}. See crewreview repo list.
error.unknownInboxItem: No review #{id} waiting in the inbox.
repo.added: Linked {id} ({url}). Review: {mode}, authors: {authors}. Signed in as {user}.
repo.orgAdded: Linked {id} ({url}): every repository in it, now and later. Review: {mode}, authors: {authors}. Signed in as {user}. {open} with open pull requests right now.
repo.none: No repositories linked yet. Add one with: crewreview repo add <url>
review.inboxed: {repo}#{number}: in the inbox as #{id} (findings: {findings}). Post it with: crewreview inbox approve {id}
review.stale: Review #{id} is out of date: the pull request has new commits. It will be reviewed again.
review.mergeOnly: {repo}#{number}: only the base moved since the last review. Nothing new to review.
review.tooLarge: {repo}#{number}: too large to review ({lines} changed lines; the limit is {limit}, limits.maxDiffLines in the settings). It's left alone until a new commit.
review.alreadyOnHost: {repo}#{number}: this commit already has a Crewreview review on the host.
skip.label: it has a skip label
skip.too-many-failures: it failed too many times on this commit
skip.settling: pushed a moment ago: waiting a few minutes for the author to finish
run.cycle: Checked {repos}: {reviewed} reviewed, {waiting} queued for the next check.
run.offline: No connection to {repos}; trying again on the next check.
run.stopping: Stopping after the current review… (Ctrl+C again to quit now)
post.delta: Focused on what changed since {sha}, the last commit reviewed.
post.leftOut: Left out (minified, generated or too large to read): {files}
post.guidelinesCut: Project rules read only in part (too long): {files}
post.reviewGuide: Followed the team's review guidance in {file}
post.droppedByVerifier.one: The verifier discarded {count} finding after checking the code.
post.droppedByVerifier.other: The verifier discarded {count} findings after checking the code.
post.alreadyDiscussed.one: {count} finding left out because the discussion already covers it.
post.alreadyDiscussed.other: {count} findings left out because the discussion already covers them.
pr.title: Crewreview · {repo}#{number}
cli.cmd.attend: Answer the reviews on one of your pull requests now.
cli.opt.attend: Attendant for your own pull requests: off, inbox or auto. Default: off.
cli.opt.polish: on: the attendant also fixes what Crewreview's reviewer found (the polish loop).
cli.opt.conflicts: on: the attendant also fixes a conflict with the base (merges it, never rebases).
cli.opt.ci: on: the attendant also fixes what turned CI red, from the failing jobs' logs.
cli.opt.include: Organization: only repositories whose name matches (*, **, ?), comma-separated.
cli.opt.exclude: Organization: leave out repositories whose name matches, comma-separated.
error.cannotWrite: {name} can't edit files, so it can't be the attendant.
error.needsWriteCheck: {name} hasn't proven it only writes inside its worktree. Run crewreview doctor --conformance first.
error.writeEscapes: {name} wrote outside its worktree in the conformance test, so it can't be the attendant.
error.signedOut: {name} isn't signed in. Sign in with: {command}
error.paused: {name} hit its usage limit and can be used again {when}. To keep going with another harness meanwhile, set harness.fallback in your config.
error.budget: Today's budget of {limit} agent runs is used up (limits.dailyRuns). The crew goes on tomorrow.
attend.settling: {repo}#{number}: new comments are still coming in; answering once they settle.
attend.fork: {repo}#{number}: comes from a fork; the attendant can't push there.
attend.pending: {repo}#{number}: answer ready in the inbox as {id} (fixed: {fixed}, replies: {replies}). Publish it with: crewreview inbox approve {id}
attend.forced.links: It adds, changes or removes a symlink or a submodule ({files}), so it always waits for you, whatever the settings or comments say.
attend.forced.sensitive: It changes sensitive files (CI, secrets, deployment, git or agent configuration, or the crew's rules), so it waits for you even in auto mode.
attend.forced.validation-failed: The project's checks still fail after a second try, so it waits for you.
attend.synced: {repo}#{number}: took in {base}, staying in line with #{parent} below it in the stack.
attend.restacked: {repo}#{number}: took in {base} now that #{parent}, below it in the stack, is merged.
attend.reReview: Asked the reviewers to look again.
attend.stale: Answer {id} is out of date: the branch moved. It will be redone.
doctor.signInHint: {name} isn't signed in. Sign in with: {command}
doctor.serviceHint: {name} works here but not for the background service ({why}). Install the service again from this terminal: crewreview service install
doctor.expiresSoon: {name}'s login ends {when}. Sign in again before that: {command}
web.noToken: Open the dashboard from your terminal; the link carries a key for this session.
web.now.noAgents: No agents working right now. They show up here, live, as soon as a review or an answer starts.
web.now.noActivity: Nothing yet. The first check runs right after the daemon starts.
web.log.noToken: no token for this host: sign in with gh or glab
web.log.answerWaiting: {repo}#{number}: answer waiting in the inbox (fixed: {fixed}, replies: {replies})
web.log.needsProof: {repo}#{number}: {name} hasn't passed its test on this computer yet; prove it in Harnesses & limits and the crew picks it up
web.log.signedOut: {repo}#{number}: {name} isn't signed in; run {command} and the crew picks it up
web.log.paused: {repo}#{number}: {name} hit its usage limit; the crew waits until {when}
web.log.budget: {repo}#{number}: today's budget of {limit} agent runs is used up; the crew goes on tomorrow
web.inbox.empty: Nothing waits for you. Reviews and answers in inbox mode land here.
web.inbox.stale: The pull request has new commits since; it will be done again.
web.inbox.retryHelp: Retry once the cause is fixed. The last attempt failed with: {error}
web.repos.addHint: A GitHub or GitLab address: a repository, or an organization or group to link every repository in it, new ones too. Crewreview uses your gh or glab login, or GH_TOKEN / GITLAB_TOKEN. New links start in inbox mode.
web.repos.orgHint: Every repository in it with open pull requests, new ones included; archived ones never. A repository linked on its own keeps its own settings.
web.repos.confirmRemove: Remove {id}? Its history stays; the crew stops watching it.
web.repos.reviewHint: Inbox waits for your approval before posting; auto posts right away.
web.repos.approveHint: When the review is clean (no findings that block, CI green, every lens done, not too large), it approves the pull request instead of only commenting. Like the settings: follows Automatic approvals in the settings for all repositories.
web.repos.attend: Answer reviews on my pull requests
web.repos.attendHint: The attendant fixes, replies and resolves. Only people who can push steer it; sensitive files always wait for you.
web.repos.polishHint: Also fix what Crewreview's own reviewer found, up to {rounds} rounds.
web.repos.conflictsHint: Merges the base into your branch and resolves the conflicts. In a stack, each branch also takes in the one below whenever it moves, and the base once that one is merged. Never rebases or force-pushes; a conflict it can't fully resolve waits for you.
web.repos.ciHint: Fixes what turned CI red on your pull request, reading the failing jobs' logs. Your checks run before anything is pushed.
web.limits.title: Limits and schedule
web.limits.settle: Wait after a push · after comments
web.limits.edit: To change these, edit {path} and restart the daemon.
cli.cmd.ui: Open the dashboard (starts the daemon if it isn't running).
cli.cmd.status: Whether the crew runs on this computer, and what it's doing.
cli.opt.retry: attend: give items that were given up another chance first.
attend.busy: {repo}#{number}: an answer is already being prepared.

service.installed: Installed as {name}: it starts now and with every login.
service.notInstalled: The service isn't installed. Install it with: crewreview service install
service.lingerHint: To keep it running after you log out: loginctl enable-linger $USER
update.installed: Updated from {from} to {to}, signature and checksum verified.
update.restart: Restart the daemon to use it (the service does this by itself).
update.notCompiled: Running from source: update with git pull instead.

desktop.notifyFix: Fixes and replies ready for your approval: {title}
desktop.updateAvailable: Crewreview {version} is available. Install it and restart?
desktop.busy: Another Crewreview is running without its dashboard. Stop it, or restart it with crewreview run.
desktop.managedUpdate: This copy came with the desktop app, which keeps it up to date.
preview.title: {link}: open pull requests: {prs}, in repositories: {repos}
preview.would: Would review now: {count}, {perCycle} per cycle (the rest in the next ones), about {runs} agent runs.
preview.own: Your open pull requests: {count}. The attendant answers their reviews when it's on.
preview.budget: Today's budget: {used} of {limit} agent runs used.
preview.note: This preview changes nothing: nothing is reviewed, posted or recorded.
web.setup.intro: Three checks and one link, and the crew starts working. Nothing is posted until you approve it.
web.setup.agentsHint: Crewreview runs the coding agents you already use, with your own login and plan. It needs one that's installed and signed in.
web.setup.agentsDefaultMissing: {name} is set for reviews but isn't ready. Sign in or install it, or choose another one with harness.default in {path}.
web.setup.agentsNone: No agent is ready yet. Install one of these and sign in, then check again.
web.setup.hostsHint: Crewreview reads pull requests and posts reviews with your gh or glab login, or GH_TOKEN / GITLAB_TOKEN. The agents never get this token.
web.setup.hostsOk: One is enough. The hosts gh and glab are signed in to show up here; another GitHub Enterprise or GitLab is checked when you link it.
web.setup.linkHint: Paste the address of a repository, or of an organization or group to watch every repository in it. Preview first to see what the crew would review right now; links start in inbox mode, so nothing is posted without you.
web.setup.next1: Every few minutes the crew looks for pull requests to review. Each review waits in the Inbox until you approve, edit or discard it.
web.setup.next2: When you trust it, switch a repository to auto in Repositories, and turn on the attendant to answer reviews on your own pull requests.
web.setup.next3: The crew works while this is running. To keep it going after you close the terminal, use the desktop app or crewreview service install.
web.setup.unreachable: The dashboard can't reach the crew. Is it still running?
account.error.bad-name: "{name}" isn't an account: use a login, or env:VARIABLE for a token kept in an environment variable.
account.error.env-unset: The environment variable {name} isn't set where the crew runs.
account.error.not-signed-in: {name} isn't signed in to gh on this computer. Run gh auth login and sign in as {name}, then gh auth switch to come back to your account.
account.error.gitlab-needs-env: glab keeps one account per host: put the token of {name} in an environment variable and use env:VARIABLE.
account.error.same-account: {name} is your own account, and nobody can approve their own pull request. Use a second account.
account.error.host: The host refused the token of {name}: {message}
account.error.keychain-missing: The token of {name} isn't in the system keychain any more. Paste it again on the Second account page.
cli.opt.account: post reviews as another account (a login signed in to gh, or env:VARIABLE), so your own pull requests can be approved; none: as you.
cli.opt.paused: on: leave the repository linked but alone (no reviews, no answers); off: back to work.
cli.opt.guidelines: More project rules for the reviewers, besides AGENTS.md and the like: paths in the repository, comma-separated; a folder gives its .md files. none: only the usual files.
cli.opt.approve: on: the review approves a clean pull request; off: it only comments; default: follow review.policy.allowApprove, the setting for all repositories.
web.repos.accountHint: Working alone? Nobody can approve their own pull request. Give the crew a second account with write access here, and its reviews, approvals included, post as that account. The step-by-step setup does it: on GitLab a group or project token, on GitHub an account you create. Empty: your own account.
web.setup.next4: Working alone? Nobody can approve their own pull request. For the crew to approve yours, give it a second account: on GitLab a group token is enough.
web.account.title: A second account
web.account.intro: Nobody can approve their own pull request. If you work alone, the crew posts its reviews as a second account, and that account's approvals count. This page does each step with you: on GitLab it takes a token, on GitHub an account you create.
web.account.s1Hint: GitHub needs a person to create an account. Open the sign-up in a private window, so this browser stays signed in as you. An email alias works (you+crew@example.com); GitHub allows one free machine account per person.
web.account.notFound: There's no account @{login} on GitHub yet.
web.account.s2Hint: With your account, the crew invites it to these repositories with write access, which its approvals need to count. On an organization's repositories an owner may have to allow it.
web.account.s3Hint: The crew starts gh's sign-in. In the private window where the new account is signed in, open the page below and type the code. gh keeps its token in your system's credential store and switches back to your account at the end.
web.account.waiting: Waiting for the code to be typed…
web.account.restored: gh is back on your account, @{user}.
web.account.err.gh-missing: gh isn't installed here: install it from cli.github.com and sign in to your own account first.
web.account.err.gh-token-env: {detail} is set where the crew runs, so gh can't add another account. Unset it, or use env:VARIABLE on the Repositories page instead.
web.account.err.wrong-account: The code was typed by another account ({who}), not @{login}. Sign in as the second account in the private window and try again.
web.account.reviewOwn: Review my own pull requests too
web.account.done: Repositories now posting as @{login}: {count}. Its approvals count.
web.account.setupLink: Set it up step by step
web.account.whereHint: Tick the repositories, organizations or groups on one host. The account is used where you tick.
web.account.nothingLinked: Nothing is linked yet. Paste the address of a repository, organization or group and the crew links it here, in Inbox mode: nothing is posted until you approve it.
web.account.gl.s2Hint: On GitLab nobody has to sign up: a group or project access token creates a bot account by itself, and the reviews are posted as that bot. A group token covers every project and subgroup in it.
web.account.gl.fExpiryHint: The longest GitLab allows. It emails you before the token expires.
web.account.gl.who: You need to be an Owner of the group or a Maintainer of the project. On gitlab.com, group and project tokens need the Premium plan; without it, create a second account and use a personal token of it:
web.account.pasteHint: It goes to the system keychain, never to a file. The crew checks who it belongs to and what it can do in each place before using it.
web.account.usedAs.one: Done: 1 place posts its reviews as @{user}.
web.account.usedAs.other: Done: {count} places post their reviews as @{user}.
web.account.usedNowhere: The token is @{user}'s, but that account has no access to the places you ticked, so nothing changed. Give it access, or tick another place.
web.account.reach.read: read only: its approvals won't count
web.account.err.keychain: The system keychain wouldn't keep the token: {message}. On a machine without a keychain, use env:VARIABLE on the Repositories page.
web.account.err.pickOne: Tick at least one place in step 1.
web.account.gh.tokenHint: In the private window, signed in as the new account, create a classic token with the repo scope (the link fills it in). It has to be classic: fine-grained tokens can't reach another person's repositories. When you paste it, the crew accepts the invitations, checks the access and keeps the token in the keychain.
web.account.gh.orgNote: For an organization ({orgs}), an owner adds the account as a member with write access to its repositories. Invitations from here are for single repositories.
web.account.reviewOwnMr: Review my own merge requests too
web.settings.title: Settings
web.settings.keepAwake: Keep the computer awake while agents work
web.settings.saved: Saved in {path}. The crew uses the new values from now on.
web.settings.autostartHint: Start Crewreview when you log in to the computer, in the menu bar, so the crew keeps working.
web.settings.autostartOnlyApp: Only in the desktop app. From a terminal, crewreview service install keeps the crew running.
web.settings.updatesHint: Once a day; you're asked before anything is installed.
web.repos.activeHint: The crew watches this repository. Paused: linked, but no reviews or answers until you turn it back on.

desktop.stale: {pr} changed since the review; it was set aside.
web.setup.proveHint: Two tiny prompts on your plan: it asks the agent to create a file while reviewing and checks it couldn't, then that it writes only inside the folder.
preview.inOrg: {total} repositories in it, subgroups included; {open} with open pull requests.
web.preview.solo: Only you open pull requests here? For the crew to review them, set Whose pull requests to everyone's after linking; for its approval to count, give it a second account.
web.limits.proveHint: Prove runs each agent for real, twice, on your plan: while reviewing it's asked to create a file and must be stopped, then it must write only inside its folder. Reviews need the read-only proof; answering reviews needs the write one. In a terminal: crewreview doctor --conformance.
status.stopped: The crew isn't running on this computer ({repos} linked).
status.start: Start it with the desktop app, crewreview run, or crewreview service install to keep it running.
status.inbox.zero: Nothing waits for you in the inbox.
status.inbox.one: 1 item waits for you in the inbox: crewreview inbox.
status.inbox.other: {count} items wait for you in the inbox: crewreview inbox.
web.team.intro: Each member of the crew is a seat: a coding agent, the model and the effort it uses, and the jobs it does. Several seats can share a job, and when one hits its usage limit the next takes over.
web.team.roleHint.review: the lenses that read each pull request
web.team.roleHint.verify: checks each finding before it's posted
web.team.roleHint.attend: fixes and replies on your pull requests
web.team.howRouted: A job takes the first seat that's free, in the order shown, or as its balance says. A seat paused at its usage limit is skipped until its limit resets.
web.team.howLegacy: No [roles] yet: each job uses the harness picked in the setup, then the fallbacks, with each harness's own model and effort.
web.team.configureHint: Seats and jobs live in {path}. An example: three seats on two plans, the reviews shared between two of them.
web.team.balanceHint: balance: "order" uses the first seat until it's paused or out of runs; "spread" shares by how much of each seat's day is left; "cheapest" picks the lowest known cost per run. A job can also name a harness ("codex") for that harness with its own settings.
task.none: No tasks yet. Start one: crewreview task "what to do" --repo <id>
task.notFound: No task {id}. See them with: crewreview task list
task.cancelled: Task {id} cancelled. Its ledger stays in the data folder.
task.nothingToApprove: Task {id} has nothing to approve now ({stage}).
task.needsRepo: {id} is an organization or group: name one repository for a task (its id, or its address).
task.created: Task {id}: the crew works on the branch {branch}, from {base}.
task.checksFailed: the project's checks failed ({command}): the next turn fixes it
task.waiting: Every seat for this job is at its usage limit; it goes on after {when}: crewreview task run
task.asks.blocked: The builder is blocked on {step}: read its handoff (crewreview task show), answer in the task, then crewreview task run
task.asks.too-many-turns: Too many turns on {step} without finishing: take a look before it goes on
task.asks.no-progress: Three turns on {step} finished nothing: take a look before it goes on
task.stage.approval: waiting for you to approve the plan
task.stage.ready: ready: waiting for you to open the pull request
task.nextApprovePlan: Approve the plan to start building: crewreview task approve {id}  (or cancel {id})
task.nextApproveOpen: Look at the branch, then open the pull request: crewreview task approve {id}
web.team.roleHint.plan: reads the repository and writes the plan of a task
web.team.roleHint.build: builds a task's steps in its own checkout
web.tasks.intro: Give the crew something to build. A planner proposes the steps, you approve them, a builder does one step at a time and commits it, the crew reviews its own branch, and once you approve again it opens the pull request.
web.tasks.placeholder: Add findUserByEmail to src/users.ts, case-insensitive, with a test
web.tasks.who: Who commits and opens the pull request
web.tasks.asYou: You: your identity and signature, your account opens it
web.tasks.asCrew: The crew's account, @{account}: you're not the author, so you can approve and merge it
web.tasks.asCrewNone: The crew's account (this repository has none yet)
web.tasks.asCrewHint: Set up a second account for this repository, and the crew can open pull requests you're free to approve.
web.tasks.auto: Don't wait for me: build and open the pull request without asking (auto)
web.tasks.started: The crew is planning it. The plan shows here when it's ready.
web.tasks.noRepos: Link a repository first (an organization or group isn't enough: a task needs one repository).
web.tasks.err.org: That's an organization or group: pick one repository.
web.tasks.err.not-found: That repository isn't linked any more.
web.tasks.confirmCancel: Cancel this task? Its branch isn't pushed; the ledger stays.
web.tasks.waiting: every seat for this job is at its usage limit; it goes on after {when}
web.tasks.approvalHint: Read the plan. If it's right, approve it and the crew starts building; if not, cancel and ask again with more detail.
web.tasks.readyHint: Built and reviewed by the crew. Look at the steps and what the review found, then open the pull request from the branch {branch}.
web.tasks.reviewSummary: {findings} finding(s) in the last round, {blocking} blocking, after {rounds} round(s).
web.tasks.cut: Cut off ({reason}): Crewreview wrote this handoff from what the agent left, and the next seat carries on.
web.tasks.ledger: Everything about this task is in tasks/{id}/ in Crewreview's data folder: the plan, every handoff and each agent's own answer.
web.log.taskPlanned: Task "{task}": a plan with {steps} steps, waiting for you.
web.log.taskChecks: Task "{task}": the project's checks failed ({command}); the next turn fixes it.
web.log.taskWaiting: Task "{task}": waiting for a seat to come back from its usage limit.
task.noCrewAccount: {id} has no crew account to act as: set one up in Repositories → Post reviews as, or use --as you.
cli.behindService: This terminal runs Crewreview {version}, but the service runs {service}. Update this copy (crewreview update) or point it at the app's.
doctor.conformanceBehind: Not testing the harnesses: this terminal runs Crewreview {version}, but the service runs {service}, and it would use these results. Update this copy (crewreview update) or test from the app (Harnesses & limits, Test the writes).
cli.linked: The terminal's crewreview ({path}) now follows the app: it replaced a separate copy, version {version}. One update covers both.
cli.relinked: The terminal's crewreview ({path}) points at the app again.
web.repos.protected: Protected files a reviewer commented on, without waiting
web.repos.protectedHint: The attendant may change protected files (CI, deployment, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) when a reviewer commented on them, to do what that comment asks. Off: that change waits for your approval, even in auto mode. On: it goes out like any fix. Secrets never change.
cli.opt.protected: approve: changes to protected files a reviewer commented on (CI, AGENTS.md…) wait for you; auto: they go out like any fix
cli.cmd.eval: Review your calibration cases at their pinned commits and score what was found and what was wrongly claimed (cases in <config>/eval).
eval.none: No calibration cases in {dir} (files ending in .case.json).
eval.summary: {cases} cases · recall {recall} · underrated {underrated} · false positives {falsePositives} · {findings} findings per review, {small} minor or nit · prompt v{prompt}
post.upgraded: raised from {from} by the verifier, see {place}
reason.not-trusted: the review isn't trusted enough to approve (see above)
trust.untrusted: ⛔ Trust: don't rely on this review alone
trust.reason.too-large: the change is too large for one review
trust.reason.major-open: a major finding is still open
post.cut: Too large to show whole, so their first hunks were shown and the rest read from the code: {files}.
post.checks: Claims and rules checked against the code: ✅ {holds} · ❌ {fails} · ❔ {unverified}
post.check.unproven: no place in the code was given
harness.reproved: {harness} updated to {version} and passed its proof again by itself.
harness.reproveFailed: {harness} updated to {version} and failed its proof; check it in Harnesses & limits.
post.verifier.confirm: The verifier checked the code and confirmed it: {reason}
post.verifier.upgrade: The verifier raised it from {from}, see {place}: {reason}
post.notRepeated.one: {count} finding already raised earlier is not repeated ({severities}).
post.notRepeated.other: {count} findings already raised earlier are not repeated ({severities}).
post.overNitCap.one: {count} nit past the limit of {cap} per review is listed below instead of on its line.
post.overNitCap.other: {count} nits past the limit of {cap} per review are listed below instead of on their lines.
post.droppedNoEvidence.one: {count} finding was dropped for citing a file or line that doesn't exist.
post.droppedNoEvidence.other: {count} findings were dropped for citing a file or line that doesn't exist.
post.droppedUnread.one: {count} finding was dropped because its lens said it couldn't read that file.
post.droppedUnread.other: {count} findings were dropped because their lens said it couldn't read those files.
attend.round.head: This round, in {sha}:
attend.round.headNoCommit: This round, with no code change:
attend.nothingBlocked.one: {repo}#{number}: nothing new. {count} item waits on you or stopped trying: try it again with --retry, or under Pull requests in the dashboard.
attend.nothingBlocked.other: {repo}#{number}: nothing new. {count} items wait on you or stopped trying: try them again with --retry, or under Pull requests in the dashboard.
web.pulls.intro: Your open pull requests the attendant works on. What waits on you is listed under each one: try it again, or mark it done if you took care of it.
web.pulls.empty: No open pull requests of yours in the repositories the attendant works on.
web.pulls.noToken: No token for this host on this computer: sign in with gh or glab.
web.pulls.draftHint: Drafts are skipped. Mark it ready for review and the crew takes it.
web.pulls.why.needs-human: The agent left it for you without saying why.
web.pulls.why.gave-up: It failed every time it was tried.
web.pulls.why.ignored: Its author can't push to the repository, or you discarded it from the inbox.
web.pulls.why.trying: A try didn't finish; it runs again at the next check.
web.pulls.dismissHint: You took care of it: it stops waiting and isn't tried again.
web.pulls.retryHint: The crew tries it again at the next check, or now with Answer now.
web.pulls.error.busy: The crew is already working on this pull request.
web.pulls.error.off: Answering reviews is off for this repository.
web.pulls.error.no-token: No token for this host on this computer.
web.pulls.error.not-found: That item or pull request isn't there any more.
web.pulls.error.other: That didn't work. Try again in a moment.
web.pulls.pausedHint: Paused: the crew doesn't work on this repository. Turn it back on under Repositories.
attend.regenerateFailed: I couldn't finish the merge with the base: `{command}`, which rebuilds the generated files, failed. The conflict is left for the owner.
